issues.display_title: Issue #1798: [Editor] Fix the Viewer Color Mode switch: unclickable and unreadable labels
issues.main_description_html:
The Dark / Light switch on the Publish panel is broken in two ways.

It cannot be clicked. Nothing happens when you click either half of the switch, so there is currently no way to change the viewer colour mode at all.

The labels disappear. Once the switch is in the Light position, the "Dark" label turns white on a white background and becomes invisible. The switch also changes colour between the two states (grey on one side, indigo on the other), so it does not look like the same control.

Expected

  • Clicking anywhere on the switch toggles between Dark and Light.
  • The switch also responds to the keyboard, with a visible focus ring.
  • Both labels stay readable in either state: the selected side sits on the coloured pill, the other side stays muted.
  • The pill keeps the same colour in both positions.

issues.display_title: Issue #1800: [Editor] Fix the Field of View dialog: collapsed layout, stray percentage bubble and footer actions
issues.main_description_html:
Problem

The Field of View dialog (General → Field of View) doesn't hold together as a window.

What you see:

  • The layout collapses — the device list (Desktop / Tablet / Mobile) is supposed to sit beside the preview. Instead the preview drops onto its own line and covers the list, so the three device options are half hidden behind the 3D view. The two halves are sized to add up to the dialog's width exactly, so any rounding pushes them apart.
  • The percentage bubble points at nothing — the reading (e.g. "77%") floats at a fixed spot near the left of the slider whatever value you set, instead of sitting over the handle.
  • The hint text — the sentence about the field of view affecting camera speed is squeezed into the narrow device column at 10px with a decorative bullet, right-aligned against everything else in the dialog.
  • The device list — labels are heading-sized (22px), and selecting one shifts its text sideways because the selected marker is added to the item's box.
  • The preview — square corners, while the dialog and the other editor dialogs are rounded.
  • Cancel / Save — sit inside the scrolling content as small pills, on a different silhouette from the buttons in Edit Frame and Edit Splash Screen, with a large empty gap above them and no divider.
  • Narrow windows — the dialog is a hard 960px, so on a smaller screen it runs past the viewport.

What it should look like

Device list on the left, preview beside it, always. The percentage bubble sits over the slider handle and moves with it. Title and hint on the full dialog width. Cancel and Save in the dialog's own footer, matching the other polished editor dialogs.

Scope

  • Put the device list and the preview on a real grid instead of two fixed widths that fill the dialog exactly; stack them on narrow screens.
  • Bind the percentage bubble's position to the slider value it already prints.
  • Move the title and hint into a header on the full width, and drop the decorative bullet.
  • Device list: label-sized type, minimum 44px rows, and a selected state that doesn't shift the label.
  • Round the preview and give it the dialog's border.
  • Move Cancel and Save into the dialog footer, on the shared editor-dialog button geometry, closed off by one divider.
  • Cap the dialog's width against the viewport.
  • Accessibility: the device options become real buttons (they were javascript:; links), with pressed state, focus rings, and labels on the −/+ steppers.

Verification

  • Open Field of View: the device list sits beside the preview, nothing overlaps.
  • Drag the slider end to end: the bubble tracks the handle at both extremes.
  • Switch Desktop / Tablet / Mobile: the label doesn't jump, and the tablet/mobile frame overlay still fits the preview.
  • Cancel and Save sit in the footer, same size as Edit Frame's, and still save/discard as before.
  • Tab through: device options and steppers take focus with a visible ring.
  • Narrow the browser: the dialog stays inside the viewport and the layout stacks.
  • Check light and dark.

issues.display_title: Issue #1804: [Style System] Capture visual baselines and CSS metrics
issues.main_description_html:
Context and goal

Create the reproducible baseline required to refactor styles without redesigning the application. The current rendered UI is the visual source of truth.

In scope

  • Record the source revision and dirty-worktree paths without modifying unrelated changes.
  • Capture representative screenshots at 1440×900 and 390×844, including light/dark themes where supported.
  • Build an Editor state matrix covering shell, tabs, General, Images/Add Artwork, Edit Frame, Objects, Text, Publish, Splash Screen, dialogs, tooltips, hover, focus, disabled, loading, and error states.
  • Include at least two Editor content fonts with materially different metrics.
  • Record CSS artifact size and the relevant selector/import/encapsulation/dialog metrics.

Preservation rules / non-goals

  • Do not change styles, markup, behavior, or user data.
  • Do not normalize dynamic canvas/video output; mask only time-dependent regions when needed.

Acceptance criteria

  • Baseline inputs, browser, viewports, themes, test data, and font-loading state are documented.
  • Screenshots and metrics can be reproduced by another engineer.
  • The Editor state matrix identifies every state needed by the pilot issues.

Dependencies and order

None. This is the Phase 0 gate for all following implementation issues.

Verification

  • Re-run the documented capture process on the same revision and compare representative output.
  • Confirm the working tree contains no unintended changes.

issues.display_title: Issue #1805: [Style System] Make Sass settings pure and order the global entry point
issues.main_description_html:
Context and goal

Make Sass configuration safe to consume from component styles and turn src/styles.scss into a predictable, import-only entry point while retaining compatibility.

In scope

  • Separate emitted selectors such as .animate and .removeScrollStyle from settings modules.
  • Keep variables, functions, and mixins side-effect-free.
  • Reduce the mixin surface to proven consumers as migration work permits.
  • Order global imports as settings, fonts, tokens, foundations, temporary compatibility, shared patterns, PrimeNG overrides, utilities, and remaining legacy compatibility.
  • Add objective guardrails to scripts/check-global-styles.test.mjs.

Preservation rules / non-goals

  • Do not remove Bootstrap or legacy compatibility in this issue.
  • Do not introduce CSS layers, Stylelint, token generators, or mass Sass-module conversion.
  • Preserve current rendering.

Acceptance criteria

  • Component-importable Sass settings emit no CSS.
  • src/styles.scss is import-only and its ordering is documented/tested.
  • Existing features retain the compatibility imports they still need.

Dependencies and order

Depends on the baseline issue. Complete before broad token or component migrations.

Verification

  • Run pnpm test:styles.
  • Run selector searches for moved helpers.
  • Run the required Angular development/SSR build according to the repository dialog-style instructions.
  • Compare affected baseline screenshots.

issues.display_title: Issue #1806: [Style System] Establish design tokens and repair layout custom properties
issues.main_description_html:
Context and goal

Create a small three-layer token system—primitive, semantic, and proven shared-component tokens—without changing the current design.

In scope

  • Introduce evidence-based --v-* primitive tokens for repeated color, spacing, radius, typography, shadow, and motion values.
  • Keep the existing concise semantic theme API such as --primary, --background, --border, and --ring.
  • Add component tokens only for stable shared primitives.
  • Correct invalid references such as var(--color-primary).
  • Give --vh, --mainHeightHeader, and --mainHeightFooter explicit ownership and safe fallbacks.

Preservation rules / non-goals

  • No parallel --color-* semantic API.
  • No blanket value normalization or speculative token catalogue.
  • Local one-off geometry remains component-owned.

Acceptance criteria

  • Tokens are defined before consumers and light/dark behavior remains correct.
  • Every new token has demonstrated consumers and a documented layer.
  • Undefined custom-property references in the migrated scope are eliminated.

Dependencies and order

Depends on pure Sass settings and global import ordering. Required before Editor typography and shared primitive migrations.

Verification

  • Run pnpm test:styles and custom-property searches.
  • Run the required Angular build.
  • Compare desktop/mobile and supported theme baselines.
